summary:
Held 2 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 4 upside misses — APP +10%, COIN +10%, AXON +10%, PLTR +9%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (GLW -13%, KLAC -12%, TER -10%, LRCX -10%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: GLW (-13.48%) — No clear news catalyst — valuation-driven pullback/profit-taking after GLW's ~390% YTD AI-optical-fiber rally pushed P/E to ~105x, amid reports of heavy June insider selling. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — GLW is tagged as industrials/specialty-glass, not tech/AI, so momentum and news-reactive strategies scoped to tech/semis sectors never scanned it despite its AI-driven re-rating this year.

top_movers.catalyst: Multi-day analyst re-rating: Raymond James initiated Strong Buy ($640 PT) on AI ad growth + Axon e-commerce rollout, extending a Q1 earnings-beat rally (~27% in a week).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: APP (mega-cap ad-tech) is ISA-eligible and sits in the T212 instrument cache, but was likely dropped by the OHLCV data-coverage post-filter (_filter_against_data_cache) for lacking recent cached bars.
top_movers.suggestion: Log tickers dropped by _filter_against_data_cache (tools/universe.py) by name, not just count, and alert when a dropped ticker is also a top gainer/loser so OHLCV backfill gaps like APP get caught fast.

top_movers.catalyst: Extended multi-day rally on Coinbase joining bank-backed 'Open USD' stablecoin coalition (Visa, Mastercard, Google, BlackRock); Benchmark/Rosenblatt/Cantor reiterated Buy w/ $208-270 targets.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — COIN sits in the crypto-exchange/digital-asset equity bucket, likely sector-blacklisted or excluded via a crypto-correlation risk filter rather than a standard cap/liquidity screen.
top_movers.suggestion: Carve out a capped crypto-adjacent equities watchlist (COIN, MSTR, HOOD) with reduced position-size limits so momentum strategies can opt in on confirmed multi-day breakouts, instead of a blanket sector exclusion.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued rally on disclosure that Trump bought up to $5M in AXON stock ahead of a $220M ICE Taser procurement notice, layered on record Q1 revenue (+34% YoY) and raised FY guidance.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AXON sits in a public-safety/government-services niche (large-cap industrials-adjacent, not core tech/momentum sector tags), so it's never scanned even as a multi-day, news-driven gainer.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'government services & public safety' sector tag to the large-cap universe builder so names like AXON (>$30B market cap) get included alongside core tech/industrials.

top_movers.catalyst: Bloomberg reported Meta is building a cloud business to sell excess AI compute capacity/models, directly rivaling AWS, Azure and Google Cloud — a major AI-monetization pivot.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: META isn't on the news-reactive strategy's tracked ticker list, so the pre-market Bloomberg scoop never generated a signal even though it's a textbook news-driven gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Expand news-reactive's universe to include mega-cap AI-infrastructure names (META, etc.) so confirmed Bloomberg/Reuters strategic-pivot scoops trigger trades, not just scheduled earnings/M&A events.

top_movers.catalyst: Robinhood hosted 'The World is Flat' event, launching the Robinhood Chain mainnet (Arbitrum-based RWA blockchain) plus EU perp-futures/UK crypto expansion, triggering GS/BTIG/Deutsche Bank target hikes to $113-125.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — HOOD is a fintech/broker-dealer name likely excluded by sector filters (crypto/blockchain-adjacent volatility) rather than by cap; the move was a scheduled product-launch/analyst-day event, not a price/volume signal any in-universe screen would have caught pre-open.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a scheduled-event watchlist gate (analyst days, product launches, blockchain mainnet launches) that temporarily admits sector-excluded fintech/crypto-adjacent names into the universe on their announced event date.

top_movers.catalyst: Expanded Nvidia sovereign-AI partnership, US Army picked Foundry for its NGC2 program, and a DA Davidson upgrade to Buy ($175 PT) extended a multi-day AI/defense-contract rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — PLTR is a mega-cap, high-multiple AI/defense name likely excluded by a valuation or sector-cap screen (e.g. max P/E or 'no pure-AI-narrative' filter), not a technical miss.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a narrow 'AI-infrastructure mega-cap' watchlist bucket with relaxed valuation caps so contract/partnership headlines (Nvidia, DoD awards) can trigger a same-day momentum entry.

top_movers.catalyst: No clear news catalyst — valuation-driven pullback/profit-taking after GLW's ~390% YTD AI-optical-fiber rally pushed P/E to ~105x, amid reports of heavy June insider selling.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — GLW is tagged as industrials/specialty-glass, not tech/AI, so momentum and news-reactive strategies scoped to tech/semis sectors never scanned it despite its AI-driven re-rating this year.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a rolling 6-month price-momentum overlay (flag any name up >100% trailing 6mo) to universe construction so re-rated 'AI-adjacent' industrials like GLW get pulled in regardless of static sector tags.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news — semiconductor-equipment sector-wide profit-taking after chips' record H1 (SOXX +82% YTD), compounded by SK Hynix HBM ramp-slowdown worries and stretched KLAC valuation (52-wk high into the drop).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely (large-cap semicap equipment, not covered) — even if it were in-universe, this was a broad sector de-rating with no earnings/news trigger, so a catalyst-driven or gap-filter bot wouldn't have flagged it pre-market.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a semicap-equipment basket (KLAC, ASML, LRCX, AMAT) to the momentum universe with a sector-relative-volume trigger, since these names now move >10% on macro/profit-taking days without idiosyncratic news.

top_movers.catalyst: Global chip-stock rout (SK Hynix -9–15%, Samsung -7–9%, Nasdaq chip selloff) hit TER just after its June 30 ATH ($487.91), unwinding a 56–64x forward P/E built on AI-testing hype.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — TER is a semiconductor test-equipment/capex name, not a mega-cap tech/AI ticker the bot tracks, so this sector-wide momentum unwind never entered its scan.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a semiconductor-equipment sub-universe (TER, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC) so momentum/mean-reversion strategies can capture AI-capex-driven swings instead of missing them entirely.

top_movers.catalyst: No single hard catalyst — broad semis profit-taking (TSMC, Micron, SanDisk, Marvell all down) after LRCX's ~154% H1 surge, plus a weak ADP jobs print and China-revenue/export-control concerns.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — LRCX is a large-cap semiconductor-equipment name whose multi-day slide (down ~4-9% on prior sessions too) is a macro/valuation unwind, not a single-day news shock a catalyst-scanner would catch.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mega-cap semiconductor-equipment names (LRCX, AMAT, KLAC) to the universe with a mean-reversion trigger on 3-day cumulative drawdown ≥15% after a prior 12-month run-up ≥100%, rather than requiring a same-day catalyst.
